main_text.p: rius capito. Cum ex ancilla puer natus esset, fructuarius eum sibi uindicabat. Intetio[?], Hic puer natus ex ancilla, in quaufumfructū[?] habeo, meus est: quéadmodū foetus cętero rū omniū animantiū. Depulfio proprietarij: Imò meus. Q.Utrius fit. R. Nō ut foetus pecorum, sic partus ancillarum in fructu est. alius enim est pecorū, alius ancillarum fructus. nam pecudū fructus, ut suum, plurimùm in sobole & progenie est positus: mulierum aut, in prudētia & ratione, hoc est artificio, industria, solertia, opere ac diligētia. nec mulierū exercēdarū fru-
[?] Words marked above are uncertain as printed.

page.notes: The running head reads IVRISCONSVLTVS and is given as IURISCONSULTUS per the u/v rule. The word "quaufumfructū" is hard to read and is only partly certain. "Intetio" is a speaker name with an uncertain accent. "Depul" at the line end is followed by "fio" on the next line, written here as one word without a printed hyphen. Speaker names Q. and R. are printed inline. The text is one continuous paragraph carried over from the previous page.
